## Rating

::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple" title="Met"}
The code runs to completion without any execution errors caused by the code itself (bugs). Errors from missing packages or file paths are scored under dependency resolution and path resolution.

[Supported by: [#80](../../sources.qmd#p80 "Replication of the morning after: report from the nottingham replication games") and [#100](../../sources.qmd#p100 "Computational and robustness reproducibility of 'UN peacekeeping and democratization in conflict-affected countries'") 'could not detect any coding errors', [#113](../../sources.qmd#p113 "Let’s talk about it: making scientific computational reproducibility easier") 'the code ran error-free', [#23](../../sources.qmd#p23 "Creating and sharing reproducible research code the workflowr way") workflowr only commits code that runs, [#115](../../sources.qmd#p115 "Similarity-based assessment of computational reproducibility in jupyter notebooks") runnability as prerequisite.]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple" title="Partially met"}
The code stops with execution errors, but the reproducer can fix them with minor, unambiguous changes that require no analytical decision (e.g. installing a missing package, adjusting a file path or working directory, a syntax change due to a newer software version), within a stated time limit (e.g. one week). Each fix is documented and reported to the authors, and the fixed code runs to completion.

[Based on: [#44](../../sources.qmd#p44 "Active maintenance: a proposal for the long-term computational reproducibility of scientific results") 'moderately trained replicator ... without substantially updating the script', [#74](../../sources.qmd#p74 "Reproducibility as a service") easy fixes = library/working-directory errors, [#128](../../sources.qmd#p128 "The reliability of replications: a study in computational reproductions") fix only when no decision is needed, [#109](../../sources.qmd#p109 "A protocol for structured robustness reproductions and replicability assessments") objective errors only, [#95](../../sources.qmd#p95 "Computational reproducibility in finance: evidence from 1,000 tests")/[#104](../../sources.qmd#p104 "Reproduce to validate: a comprehensive study on the reproducibility of economics research") one-week budget, [#52](../../sources.qmd#p52 "CODECHECK: an open science initiative for the independent execution of computations underlying research articles during peer review to improve reproducibility") record and report, [#14](../../sources.qmd#p14 "An empirical analysis of journal policy effectiveness for computational reproducibility") 'reproducible after tweaking'.]{.source-note}
:::
::: {.callout-important appearance="simple" title="Not met"}
The code stops with errors that cannot be fixed without substantial rewriting, without decisions only the authors can make, or without the authors' help; or the errors remain unresolved after the time limit. The errors are recorded and returned to the authors.

[Based on: [#44](../../sources.qmd#p44 "Active maintenance: a proposal for the long-term computational reproducibility of scientific results") 'moderately trained replicator ... without substantially updating the script', [#74](../../sources.qmd#p74 "Reproducibility as a service") easy fixes = library/working-directory errors, [#128](../../sources.qmd#p128 "The reliability of replications: a study in computational reproductions") fix only when no decision is needed, [#109](../../sources.qmd#p109 "A protocol for structured robustness reproductions and replicability assessments") objective errors only, [#95](../../sources.qmd#p95 "Computational reproducibility in finance: evidence from 1,000 tests")/[#104](../../sources.qmd#p104 "Reproduce to validate: a comprehensive study on the reproducibility of economics research") one-week budget, [#52](../../sources.qmd#p52 "CODECHECK: an open science initiative for the independent execution of computations underlying research articles during peer review to improve reproducibility") record and report, [#14](../../sources.qmd#p14 "An empirical analysis of journal policy effectiveness for computational reproducibility") 'reproducible after tweaking'.]{.source-note}
:::


::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" title="Not applicable"}
Never.
:::

**[#109](../../sources.qmd#p109)** A protocol for structured robustness reproductions and replicability assessments · *injunctive*

> "For all other errors due to missing data or incorrect code, document these problems if you were able to identify them, but do not yet attempt to solve them." (p. 4–5); explicit list of objective errors includes: "variable misspecification, coding switcheroo, outlier management, missing data handling, sensitive commands such as merging, appending, reshaping, and dropping data." *Note:* The paper defines a two-stage procedure: (1) first run without corrections and document errors; (2) then in Code Inspection, identify and correct objective errors only, explicitly distinguished from subjective analytical decisions. The distinction between objective errors and analytical choices is central to this criterion. Strictly manual.

**[#131](../../sources.qmd#p131)** Guide for Accelerating Computational Reproducibility in the Social Sciences · *injunctive*

> Whenever code is available in the reproduction package, you should be able to debug those scripts. There are at least five types of debugging that can improve the reproduction package:
>
> Code cleaning: Simplify the instructions (e.g., by wrapping repetitive steps in a function or a loop) or remove redundant code (i.e., old code that was commented out) while keeping the original output intact.
>
> Performance improvement: Replace the original instructions with new ones that perform the same tasks but take less time (e.g., choose one numerical optimization algorithm over another while still obtaining the same results).
>
> Adding unit tests: Add if/then statements after a code chunk or section (more or less every 100 lines of code) where you test that variables or statistics are computing as expected. If the value has changed, create a warning message that mentions what object has changed.
>
> Environment set up: Modify the code to include correct paths to files, specific versions of software, and instructions to install missing packages or libraries.
>
> Correcting errors: A coding error will occur when a section of the code in the production package executes a procedure that is in direct contradiction with the intended procedure expressed in the documentation (i.e., paper or code comments). For example, an error will occur if the paper specifies that the analysis is performed on a population of males, but the code restricts the analysis to females only..
